mutation_context: ABCC8 splice mutation c.4412-2A>G, rare patient-specific modifier variant associated with moyamoya/pulmonary vasculopathy in NF1, frequency unknown/not population-wide
annotation_note: ABCC8 acts here as a vascular-modifier biomarker for pulmonary/moyamoya risk in a rare genotype, not a Schwann-cell drug target; K-ATP channel pharmacology (sulfonylureas) would act on vascular smooth muscle, a stromal compartment.
ABL1 is a druggable kinase (imatinib/dasatinib/nilotinib class) acting on the Schwann-lineage tumour cell, not restricted to a specific NF2-SWN genotype.
ACSL3 is a druggable enzyme exploitable as synthetic-lethal ferroptosis induction in NF2-null schwannoma cells themselves, relevant to essentially all NF2-SWN tumors, not a distinct genotype subset.
ADAM9 is overexpressed in VS Schwann cells with a secreted isoform correlating with hearing loss, supporting prognostic biomarker use over direct drug targeting.
AKT/mTOR is directly druggable (e.g. rapalogs, AKT inhibitors) in Schwann-lineage MPNST cells downstream of RRM2, relevant to all NF1-driven MPNST, not tumor microenvironment.
AKT/mTOR is directly druggable (MK2206, rapamycin/analogs) and acts on the NF1-null glioma tumor cell itself, reducing Ccl5; germline NF1 loss affects essentially all patients.

AKT is directly druggable (allosteric/ATP-competitive inhibitors exist) and mediates NF1-loss-driven proliferation in both tumor Schwann/glial cells and endothelium; germline NF1 loss affects essentially all patients.
ALDH1A1 is a TAZ-driven tumor-cell-intrinsic marker of NF2-null Schwann/meningothelial cells; no approved or clinical-stage direct inhibitor exists, so it functions as a biomarker.
ALK is directly druggable with approved/clinical-stage inhibitors; mechanism acts on NF1-deficient tumor cells via RAS/ERK, not tumor microenvironment, and applies broadly, not to a genotype subset.

AMPD3 knockdown affects ERK/proliferation/apoptosis in Schwann-lineage tumor cells and is elevated in NF1 tissue/plasma, making it useful as a biomarker despite early-stage siRNA-only evidence of direct pharmacology.

ANXA3 is upregulated in NF2-null meningioma tumour cells and drives proliferation; no established inhibitor exists, so it functions as a proliferation/prognostic marker and intrinsic tumour-cell target, not TME or mutation-subset restricted.
Apocynin is a direct NADPH-oxidase (NCF1/p47phox-CYBB) inhibitor acting on ROS-driven macrophage infiltration in vessel wall, a microenvironmental/vascular mechanism, not tumor-cell intrinsic.
AR acts in the tumour cell, where it binds the VEGFA promoter; the angiogenic effect on stroma is downstream of that, so the drug target is tumour-intrinsic.
ATR is directly druggable (AZD6738, VE-821 are clinical-stage inhibitors) acting on the tumour cell itself, showing synthetic-lethal efficacy in NF1 glioma/MPNST lines.
AURKA is a druggable kinase (MLN8237/alisertib is clinical-stage) acting directly on NF1-mutant MPNST tumor cells, not a mutation-restricted biomarker or stromal target.
Used here as a serum biomarker tracking tumor burden, not a drug target; AXL itself is druggable (e.g. bemcentinib) but acts mainly via TME/endothelial-immune signaling.

BDNF is a secreted neurotrophic ligand acting on nerve-resident/stromal cells (e.g., mast cells, axons) and correlates with disease activity, making it more useful as a pharmacodynamic biomarker than a direct drug target.
BET proteins are directly druggable by clinical-stage BET bromodomain inhibitors, acting on MPNST tumor cells themselves, not restricted to a NF1 subgenotype or the microenvironment.

Bevacizumab is an approved anti-VEGFA antibody acting on tumour-associated endothelium/angiogenesis, not the NF2-null Schwann cell itself, benefiting essentially all NF2-SWN vestibular schwannoma patients.
Survivin is directly druggable (YM155, LQZ-7I) in NF1-null Schwann-lineage tumor cells themselves, not a stratifying marker or microenvironment target.

mutation_context: BMPR2 p.M365I variant, single NF1 patient case report; population frequency unknown/not established
annotation_note: Partial-loss-of-function variant found in one patient acts as a modifier/stratification marker for pulmonary phenotype, not a direct druggable lesion.
BORC is a lysosomal-trafficking complex directly targeted by compound Y102 in NF1-deficient Schwann-lineage tumor cells (PN, MPNST, glioma), acting on the tumor cell itself.
Cav2.2 is a druggable ion channel (ziconotide precedent) driving CGRP release from sensory neurons, relevant to all Nf1+/- pain, not tumor/stroma.
CCL2 is a druggable chemokine (CCR2/CCL2 axis has clinical-stage antagonists) that acts on macrophage recruitment in the DRG microenvironment, not the tumor cell itself.
CCL5 is a druggable chemokine (CCR5 antagonists exist) acting mainly via macrophage recruitment/autocrine signaling, so stromal/TME mechanism dominates despite some tumor-intrinsic autocrine role.
CCR5 has approved/clinical-stage antagonists (e.g. maraviroc) and here acts on macrophage proliferation in the cNF microenvironment, not the Schwann-cell tumor cell.

Approved anti-PD-L1/PD-1 checkpoint agents exist, but here CD274 is used as a serum stratification biomarker and would act on tumor-infiltrating T cells/immune microenvironment, not the Schwann-lineage tumor cell.
CD44 marks fibrotic/ECM-remodeled Schwann cells linked to bevacizumab resistance and macrophage-SCP crosstalk, favoring biomarker/stromal-signaling use over direct tumor-cell drug target.
CD74/MIF axis is druggable (anti-CD74 or MIF antagonists) but acts mainly via macrophages/DCs and stromal signaling in the PN microenvironment, not the Schwann-cell tumor clone itself.
CDK4/6 has approved clinical-stage inhibitors (e.g., palbociclib) acting directly on hyperproliferative Schwann-lineage MPNST tumor cells, not restricted to a genetic subgroup.

CDKN1A (p21) is a cell-cycle/senescence effector best used as a proliferation or pharmacodynamic biomarker; no direct inhibitor/activator exists, and it acts within the Schwann-lineage tumour cell, not stroma.

mutation_context: CDKN2A/9p21 (p16) homozygous deletion, found in a subset of atypical neurofibromas and most MPNSTs, not present in benign plexiform neurofibromas
annotation_note: CDKN2A loss is a tumor-suppressor deletion best used as a diagnostic/prognostic marker of malignant progression, not a druggable target, and acts within the Schwann-cell lineage.

mutation_context: CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion/loss in neurofibroma-to-MPNST progression; reported in ~simple majority of MPNSTs but not present in benign neurofibromas or germline NF1 alone
annotation_note: CDKN2A/B loss is a deletion event with no direct drug target, best used to flag malignant transformation risk and select CDK4/6-inhibitor therapy in tumor cells.

mutation_context: CDKN2A/CDKN2B homozygous deletion at 9p21, found in subset of atypical neurofibroma (ANNUBP) and most MPNST, not in benign NF1 neurofibromas
annotation_note: CDKN2B is a tumor-suppressor deletion marking malignant progression (ANNUBP to MPNST), useful for stratification but not a direct drug target.
CENPF is a proliferation/mitotic marker overexpressed in MPNST, useful prognostically but not a validated direct drug target, and acts within tumor cells, not stroma.
STING agonists could reactivate suppressed cGAS-STING signaling directly in NF2-null schwannoma tumour cells; germline NF2 loss defines the disease, not a subset.
CIP2A is an oncogenic PP2A inhibitor lacking approved/clinical-stage direct inhibitors, more useful as a prognostic biomarker of meningioma aggressiveness than a drug target.
CPA4 is a secreted carboxypeptidase with no approved or clinical-stage inhibitors, so it is more useful as a tumour marker than a drug target.
ICG-001 directly inhibits CBP/CREB-β-catenin transcriptional activity in NF2-mutant meningioma tumor cells, real pharmacology not merely a biomarker or stromal mechanism.
CRL4-DCAF1 is directly druggable (MLN3651 inhibits it, restoring LATS1/2 and killing Merlin-deficient meningioma cells), acting on the tumor cell itself in essentially all NF2-SWN patients.
CRMP2 is druggable directly (t-CNRP1 peptide disrupts CRMP2-Cav2.2 to block CGRP release); relevant to all NF1 patients via germline neurofibromin loss, acting on sensory neurons, not TME.
CSF1/CSF1R has clinical-stage inhibitors (e.g. pexidartinib) and would act on macrophages within the VS microenvironment, not the schwannoma cell itself.
CSF1R inhibitors (e.g. pexidartinib) target tumor-associated microglia/macrophages driving OPG growth, not the Schwann/glioma cell itself, and apply broadly to NF1-OPG.
GM-CSF correlates with VS tumor volume, suggesting biomarker use; as a drug target it would act on tumor-associated macrophages/microenvironment, not schwannoma cells themselves.

GM-CSFR-α marks PNF-infiltrating myeloid cells (biomarker of macrophage/DC infiltration) but genetic deletion failed to reduce tumor burden, arguing against it as a TME drug target despite compartment fit.

CSF2RB (GM-CSFRβc) is druggable on tumor-associated macrophages/dendritic cells, acting on the PNF microenvironment rather than Schwann-lineage tumor cells; relevant to all NF1 PNF, not a mutation-restricted subset.
CXCL10-CXCR3 signaling recruits immune cells (T cells/DCs) in the microenvironment; chemokine axis is a pharmacodynamic/initiation marker rather than a validated drug target itself.
CXCR3 antagonists exist and target immune cells (T cells/DCs/macrophages) in the tumor microenvironment, not the Nf1-null Schwann cell itself.
HMGCR/SQLE are directly druggable (statins, terbinafine) in tumour cells; relevant to germline NF1 loss broadly, not a subset genotype.
Decorin is a secreted ECM proteoglycan marking Schwann/stromal subpopulations; useful as expression biomarker, not a direct drug target.
DLK1 lacks credible direct inhibitors; overexpression on Schwann-lineage MPNST cells makes it chiefly a prognostic/biomarker candidate, though its immunosuppressive TME effects are secondary.
DLX5 is a developmental transcription factor lacking direct inhibitors; best used as a lineage/expression marker in MPNST tumour cells rather than a druggable target.
CRMP2 is directly targeted by (S)-lacosamide in the NF1 pain programme that generated this row, so it is a drug target, not only a pathway marker.

PRC2/EED loss is a recurrent co-occurring lesion (with CDKN2A/TP53) marking malignant progression in NF1 MPNST, better used to stratify/classify tumors than as a direct drug target on Schwann-lineage cells.
EGFR is druggable on the tumor cell itself (lapatinib clinically active in NF2 VS/meningioma); relevant broadly via NF2-loss-driven EGFR upregulation, not a specific subset mutation.
HuR is overexpressed (not mutated) in MPNST tumor cells themselves; genetic/pharmacological inhibition is directly antitumor, a real druggable mechanism relevant across NF1-MPNST.
EPHA2 is druggable (dasatinib inhibits pEPHA2/pAkt) and acts directly on NF2-null Schwann tumor cells, not the microenvironment; relevant to all NF2-driven VS.
EphA2 is directly druggable (brigatinib inhibition reduces AKT/ERK) in NF2-deficient meningioma tumor cells; relevant to all NF2-SWN patients, not a stromal target.
pEPHB1 is a druggable activated kinase in NF2-null meningioma cells, targetable by dasatinib directly on the tumour cell, relevant to all NF2-loss meningiomas.
ErbB2 is overexpressed/activated in NF2-related meningioma and vestibular schwannoma tumour cells and is directly druggable by lapatinib, a clinical-stage inhibitor.

mutation_context: EVI2B lies within the NF1 microdeletion region, present in ~5-10% of NF1 patients with large germline NF1 gene deletions
annotation_note: EVI2B is a co-deleted passenger gene in NF1 microdeletion syndrome, useful only for genotype stratification, not a druggable target.
FAIM2 is an anti-apoptotic membrane protein with no approved or clinical-stage inhibitors, better suited as a prognostic/resistance biomarker in MPNST.
FAK1/PTK2 is directly druggable (brigatinib inhibits p-FAK) in NF2-null Schwann/meningioma tumor cells themselves, relevant to all NF2 patients, not a stromal target.
FER is a druggable kinase directly inhibited by brigatinib in NF2-deficient schwannoma and meningioma tumor cells, not merely a biomarker.

FGF1/2 are druggable secreted ligands (FGFR inhibitors exist) acting paracrine from MSC2 Schwann cells onto stromal/receptor-bearing microenvironment populations in PN, not a tumor-intrinsic mutation-defined marker.
FGFR1-4 are druggable (approved pan-FGFR inhibitors exist), but here the proposed mechanism is paracrine FGF signaling onto stromal cells, not the Schwann-cell tumor itself.
FGFR1-4 are directly druggable (approved/clinical-stage pan-FGFR inhibitors exist) and act on the meningioma tumour cell itself, not stroma.
FLT1/VEGFR1 is druggable (e.g. bevacizumab, multi-kinase inhibitors) and acts on tumour-associated vasculature/angiogenesis, not the schwannoma cell itself.
FOXM1 is a druggable transcription factor (e.g. thiostrepton) acting in Merlin-deficient meningioma tumor cells via Wnt/β-catenin signaling, relevant to essentially all NF2-SWN meningiomas.
G6PD is a druggable metabolic enzyme; synthetic lethality exploits NF2-null Schwann cell redox dependence, acting directly on tumor cells, not a subset mutation or stroma.

GDNF-neutralizing antibody is a credible pharmacological approach targeting Schwann/satellite glia-secreted ligand driving pain, a stromal/nerve microenvironment mechanism relevant to all Nf1-deficient patients.
GFRα1 is a neuronal receptor druggable by knockdown/antagonism to block GDNF-driven pain signaling; not a tumor-cell or biomarker target, relevant to all NF1 patients.
GHSR is a GPCR with ghrelin-axis ligands (e.g., ghrelin mimetics/antagonists) but here it's evidenced only as an IHC correlate of tumor volume, favoring biomarker use on Schwann-lineage tumor cells.
Fimepinostat is a clinical-stage HDAC (HDAC2) inhibitor acting directly on schwannoma tumor cells, relevant to NF2-SWN broadly, not TME or a specific subtype.
HDAC11 has a potent selective inhibitor (FT895) acting directly on MPNST tumor cells via mitochondrial disruption, relevant across NF1 patients, not a specific genotype subset.
HDAC2 is druggable by clinical-stage/approved pan-HDAC inhibitors acting directly on schwannoma tumour cells, relevant to NF2-SWN generally, not a specific genotype subset.

HIF-1α here is a pathway readout of mitochondrial impairment after FT895 treatment, not a shown driver, making it better suited as a pharmacodynamic biomarker than a direct drug target on MPNST Schwann-lineage cells.
HIF-1α drives MPNST tumor cell survival under hypoxia and is directly druggable (chetomin/siRNA), acting on tumor cells, not stroma, across NF1 patients generally.
HMGB1 is a druggable secreted alarmin; mechanism acts via neuronal CCL2 and macrophage recruitment to DRG, a microenvironment/immune pain pathway, not tumor-cell-intrinsic.

mutation_context: HRAS G12V activating mutation; rare in NF1 MPNST, not present in most patients
annotation_note: G12V-mutant HRAS drives tumor-cell Ras/Erk signaling via Gal-1; disruptable, restricted to HRAS-mutant MPNST subset.
Hyaluronan is extracellular matrix built by HAS/HYAL enzymes; targeting it (e.g., HAS inhibitors, PEGPH20) acts on tumour stroma/microenvironment, not schwannoma cells directly.
IAP inhibitors (e.g. Smac mimetics targeting survivin/XIAP) are clinical-stage direct pharmacology acting on the MPNST tumor cell itself, relevant broadly, not a defined genotype subset.

mutation_context: IDH1 R132 hotspot mutation, found in this patient's incidental cholangiocarcinoma, not an NF1-associated lesion and not present in NF1 patients generally
annotation_note: IDH1 mutation is a tumor-intrinsic biomarker selecting ivosidenib therapy for an incidental cholangiocarcinoma, unrelated to NF1 pathogenesis.
IGF1R-axis is druggable; microglial IGF1 signals to Schwann/glioma cells, relevant to all NF1 patients.
IL-6 has approved inhibitors (tocilizumab/siltuximab) and acts on DRG macrophages/pain signaling, a microenvironment/neuroimmune mechanism, not the Schwann-lineage tumor cell itself.
IRF3 is druggable via disrupting NF2m-IRF3 condensates/restoring TBK1 signaling in schwannoma cells, relevant to all NF2-null VS, not immune/stromal.

KDM2B is a histone demethylase/epigenetic regulator implicated in MPNST biology; useful as a lineage/epigenetic marker, with only early-stage epigenetic inhibitor pharmacology against the tumor cell itself.
KIF18A is a mitotic kinesin druggable in tumor cells themselves; emerging KIF18A inhibitors exist, and here it drives MPNST cell aneuploidy, not TME or genotype-restricted biology.
Imatinib is a credible direct KIT inhibitor, but the NF1 mechanism is SCF/c-kit+ mast cell recruitment, i.e. microenvironment-driven tumorigenesis.
KITLG/c-kit signaling is druggable (e.g., imatinib) and acts on tumor-associated mast cells in the microenvironment, not the Nf1-null Schwann cell itself.
KRAS is directly druggable (pan-KRAS BI-2865) and mediates MAPK signaling in NF1-null Schwann cell tumors, not genotype-restricted since NF1 loss is universal in plexiform neurofibroma.
KSR1 is a scaffold protein lacking direct inhibitors; overexpression marks Merlin-deficient meningioma tumour cells, not stroma.
KYNU marks a macrophage subset driving tryptophan/IDO1-linked immunosuppression; better used as a biomarker of this TME state than as a direct drug target itself.
Gal-1 directly chaperones Ras at the tumor cell membrane; LLS30 inhibits this pocket, acting on Schwann-lineage MPNST cells, not stroma.

mutation_context: Germline LZTR1 inactivating mutations in ~40% of sporadic and up to 85% of familial (with SMARCB1) schwannomatosis; not present in all patients
annotation_note: LZTR1 loss is a tumour-suppressor deletion/mutation acting cell-intrinsically in Schwann-lineage cells, used diagnostically to stratify schwannomatosis rather than as a direct drug target.
MEK1/2 has approved inhibitors (selumetinib) with direct pharmacology on RAS-pathway-driven Schwann-lineage tumor cells, relevant to essentially all NF1-driven tumors.

MEK/RAF inhibitors (e.g., trametinib, selumetinib) directly and effectively target MAPK pathway activation driven by germline NF1 loss in essentially all NF1 patients, acting on the tumor cell itself.

MAPK1/3 (ERK1/2) are directly druggable downstream RAS-MAPK effectors relevant to all NF1 patients via neurofibromin loss, acting in Schwann-lineage/neuronal cells, not restricted to a subgroup or the microenvironment.
ERK1/2 is a druggable downstream RAS-MAPK effector active in essentially all NF1/NF2-driven tumours, acting directly on Schwann-lineage tumour cells; MEK/ERK inhibitors are clinical-stage.

mutation_context: MDM2 amplification, a subset of NF1-associated GISTs (SDH-competent/wild-type KIT-driven subset), not present in all NF1-GIST
annotation_note: MDM2 inhibitors (e.g., idasanutlin) directly antagonize p53 degradation in MDM2-amplified tumor cells, relevant only to that molecular subset.
ME1 loss is a metabolic vulnerability marker in NF2-null Schwann tumor cells reflecting synthetic lethality with G6PD, not a direct drug target with credible inhibitors.
MET is a directly druggable RTK (cabozantinib target) active on Schwann-lineage plexiform neurofibroma cells, relevant broadly in Nf1-driven PN rather than a specific subset genotype.
MIF is druggable (clinical-stage MIF/CD74 inhibitors exist), but mechanism is SCP-to-macrophage signaling, acting on the microenvironment rather than tumor cells.
MiRNA with no direct pharmacological agent or validated mechanism reported; best suited as a diagnostic/prognostic marker for MPNST in NF1 tumours.

MMP9 is a secreted protease driven by schwannoma cells themselves (TNF-α induced) with credible small-molecule/antibody inhibitors, so it acts on the tumor cell/ECM invasion axis, not primarily stroma.

mutation_context: MN1 overexpression/amplification reported in a subset of NF1-associated MPNSTs; exact population frequency not established
annotation_note: MN1 is a nuclear transcriptional coregulator with no ligand-binding pocket or clinical inhibitor, better suited as a prognostic/stratification marker in MPNST subsets.

mutation_context: MRVI1 p.P186S variant, reported in single NF1 patients with moyamoya syndrome; frequency not established, not present in most NF1 patients
annotation_note: MRVI1 P186S is a rare candidate modifier variant linked to moyamoya vasculopathy risk stratification in NF1, not a druggable tumour-cell target.

mutation_context: MTAP/CDKN2A co-deletion, ~85% of MPNSTs; not present in benign neurofibromas
annotation_note: MTAP loss marks malignant transformation; deletion itself undruggable, though it creates PRMT5-inhibitor synthetic-lethal vulnerability.
mTOR is directly druggable (everolimus, AZD2014) acting on the tumor cell itself in NF1/NF2-driven tumors, relevant across essentially all patients with these manifestations.
MYC is an undruggable transcription factor amplified/overexpressed in NF1-GIST progression, functioning as a prognostic/proliferation marker rather than a direct drug target on tumour cells.
NF1 is a tumour-suppressor loss (neurofibromin, a RAS-GAP) with nothing to inhibit; it defines the disease and is not druggable, only useful as a lesion/classification marker.
NF2/merlin loss is a tumour-suppressor deletion with no direct drug target, but it defines NF2-SWN itself and guides use of downstream MEK/PI3K/neddylation inhibitors in Schwann-lineage tumour cells.
NF-κB inhibitors (e.g. IKK/proteasome-based) directly target pathway activation in Nf1-null Schwann cell lineage cells, relevant to essentially all PN, not immune/stromal compartment.

NFKB1/NF-κB pathway activation reflects tumor-cell signaling dysregulation in MPNST, more useful for stratification/prognosis than as a direct drug target given lack of credible direct NFKB1 inhibitors.
NGF is druggable via clinical-stage anti-NGF antibodies (tanezumab-class), but in OPG it likely acts on microenvironment/neuronal signaling rather than the glial tumour cell itself.
Nirogacestat is a clinical-stage gamma-secretase inhibitor directly blocking Notch processing in MPNST tumour cells, relevant broadly via PRC2 loss rather than a specific subset mutation.
NRG1 is a paracrine ligand signaling from axons/stroma to Schwann cells via ErbB2/3, so targeting it hits microenvironmental signaling.
DFMO is a credible clinical-stage direct ODC1 inhibitor acting on tumor Schwann-lineage cells, though ODC activity also serves as a stratification biomarker.

Clemastine promotes oligodendrocyte precursor differentiation/remyelination, a repurposed antimuscarinic with credible direct pharmacology on the glial lineage, not tumor stroma or a genotype-restricted subset.
PAK has clinical-stage inhibitors (PF-3758309) acting directly on merlin-deficient Schwann tumor cells, relevant to all NF2-SWN patients, not a specific subgenotype.
PAK1/2 have clinical-stage inhibitors (FRAX-1036, G-5555, NVS-PAK1-1) acting directly on NF2-null schwannoma tumour cells, relevant to essentially all NF2 patients, not a stromal target.
PARP1 is directly druggable (olaparib) acting on tumor Schwann-cell lineage via synthetic lethality with MEK inhibition, relevant broadly to NF1-MPNST, not a specific subclone genotype.

mutation_context: PDGFRA activating mutations/amplification in GIST subset; rare in NF1-associated GIST vs KIT-mutant majority
annotation_note: PDGFRA has approved TKIs (imatinib); relevant mainly to PDGFRA-mutant GIST, not all NF patients.

PDLIM2 is a Merlin-deficiency-driven proliferation dependency in tumor cells themselves (schwannoma/meningioma), with knockdown data supporting it as a direct pharmacological target, not merely a marker.
RKIP itself is drugged directly by TβR1-blocking small molecules (PRG-N-01) that restore RKIP in NF2-deficient Schwann cells, relevant to all Merlin-null schwannomas.
PI3K inhibitors (e.g., pictilisib) directly target hyperactivated PI3K in tumour Schwann/glioma cells downstream of NF1/NF2 loss, present in essentially all patients.
PI3K-AKT-mTOR is directly druggable (e.g. mTOR inhibitors) acting on neuronal/glial signaling driving cognitive deficits in germline NF1 loss, relevant to essentially all patients.
PI3K/AKT/GSK3β is druggable downstream of NF1 loss with clinical-stage PI3K/AKT inhibitors, acting directly on the Schwann-cell-lineage tumour cell in essentially all NF1 patients.
PLK1 is directly druggable (clinical-stage inhibitor BI6727) and acts on the Schwann-lineage MPNST tumor cell itself, causing mitotic arrest, not the microenvironment.
POSTN is a marker of an SCP-like/injury-response Schwann cell state and matrix-associated stroma, useful for tumor classification rather than direct drug targeting.
PP2A activity is pharmacologically restorable (e.g. FTY720) directly in Schwann-lineage tumor cells, relevant to essentially all NF1/NF2 neurofibromas, not immune/stromal.

mutation_context: Biallelic somatic SV-mediated inactivation of EED/SUZ12 (PRC2 loss), found in a subset (~50-80%) of MPNSTs, not all NF1 tumors
annotation_note: PRC2 loss is a tumor-suppressor lesion (nothing to inhibit) best used as a prognostic/stratification biomarker, acting tumor-cell-intrinsically in a genomically-defined MPNST subset.

mutation_context: MTAP deletion/loss (co-deleted with CDKN2A) in MPNST and ANNUBP, seen in subset of NF1 tumors, exact NF1-population frequency not well established
annotation_note: PRMT5 inhibitors act directly on MTAP-deficient Schwann-lineage tumor cells via synthetic lethality, not stroma; restricted to MTAP-deleted subset.
PROS1-AXL is a secreted-ligand/receptor axis signaling from stromal/immune cells to Schwann-lineage cells; AXL inhibitors exist, so mechanism is microenvironmental, not tumor-cell-intrinsic.
PTEN loss is a tumor-suppressor deletion/downregulation acting on Schwann-lineage tumor cells, useful as a stratification biomarker for TOR-inhibitor response, not itself druggable.
FAK is a readout in this corpus's meningioma paper, but FAK inhibitors are clinical stage in NF2-mutant meningioma, so the target itself is druggable.
SHP2 has a credible clinical-stage direct inhibitor (SHP099) acting on RAS-MAPK in NF1-null Schwann/MPNST tumor cells, relevant to essentially all NF1 patients, not tumor microenvironment.
PTPRS is a downregulated tumour-suppressor phosphatase in Schwann-lineage PNF cells; no direct activator exists, so its value is as a prognostic/recurrence biomarker, not a drug target.
RABL6A is an oncogenic GTPase acting cell-intrinsically in Schwann-lineage tumor cells; loss sensitizes to CDK4/6 inhibitors, a real pharmacological handle, not just a marker.
RAD51 is directly druggable (e.g., RI-1) to block HR repair in tumor Schwann/glioma cells, sensitizing them to radiation; relevant broadly, not TME.

RAS itself is now directly druggable (KRAS G12C/G12D inhibitors, pan-RAS/SOS1 agents) and acts on tumor Schwann-lineage cells via MAPK hyperactivation, relevant across NF1/SWN broadly, not a restricted subgroup.
MEK inhibitors (e.g. selumetinib) directly inhibit RAS/MAPK pathway signaling in NF1-null Schwann cell tumors; germline NF1 loss affects essentially all patients.
RAS-MAPK is directly druggable (MEK inhibitors like selumetinib are approved in NF1) and pathway is hyperactivated in essentially all NF1 patients via germline loss.
RAS/MAPK is the core signaling output of NF1 loss itself, druggable directly (e.g. MEK inhibitors like selumetinib), acting on the tumour cell, relevant to essentially all NF1 patients.
RB/E2F is druggable indirectly via HuR or CDK4/6 inhibitors acting on MPNST tumour cells themselves, relevant to essentially all NF1-MPNST regardless of specific genotype.

RB1 is wild-type but functionally inactivated via CDK hyperactivation; the druggable node is CDK4/6, not RB1 itself, so RB1 status serves as a pathway/biomarker indicator on the Schwann-lineage tumor cell.
RECQL4 knockdown directly sensitizes MPNST/glioma tumor cells to ATR inhibitors, a genuine synthetic-lethal pharmacological vulnerability, not just a stratification marker.

mutation_context: RNF213 p.R4810K variant; found in ~95% of East Asian moyamoya patients but only a subset of NF1 patients with moyamoya syndrome
annotation_note: R4810K is a vasculopathy susceptibility marker for moyamoya risk stratification in NF1, not a validated drug target; RNF213 E3 ligase biology lacks credible direct inhibitors.
RRM2 is overexpressed in MPNST tumor cells and has clinical-stage direct inhibitors, so real pharmacology outweighs its prognostic biomarker use.
SCF/KIT signaling drives mast cell recruitment in plexiform neurofibroma stroma; imatinib targets this KIT axis therapeutically.
SCN9A (Nav1.7) is a validated direct drug target for pain signaling in sensory neurons, relevant to NF1 pain broadly, not tumor microenvironment or a mutation subset.
SERPINB4 is a serpin overexpressed in MPNST tissue, useful as a diagnostic/classification marker of tumor cells; no established direct inhibitor exists.
SFKs are directly druggable (dasatinib) in Schwann-cell-lineage VS tumor cells, relevant to essentially all NF2 patients, not a specific tumor microenvironment mechanism.
SGK1 is an mTORC2-driven kinase druggable by SGK1 inhibitors, acting in NF2-null tumour cells themselves, not restricted to a patient subgroup or the microenvironment.

mutation_context: PRC2-deficient (SUZ12/EED-loss) NF1-mutant MPNST subgroup, a minority of MPNSTs
annotation_note: SHH/SMO is druggable (vismodegib/sonidegib precedent) and acts on the Schwann-lineage tumor cell, but activation is restricted to PRC2-deficient NF1 MPNST subgroup.

mutation_context: Germline SMARCB1 mutation defines a schwannomatosis subset (~40-50% of non-NF2, non-LZTR1 SWN), not present in all SWN patients
annotation_note: SMARCB1 loss (INI1 loss) is a tumour-suppressor deletion/diagnostic marker with no direct inhibitor target, restricted to SMARCB1-mutant schwannomatosis patients.
SOS1 is a direct pharmacological target (clinical-stage SOS1 inhibitors exist) acting on RAS/MAPK-driven NF1-null Schwann-lineage tumor cells, though SOS2 compensation limits monotherapy efficacy.
SOS2 is a druggable RasGEF paralog acting cell-intrinsically in Schwann-lineage tumor cells, relevant via NF1 loss, not a patient subset.
SOX10 is a lineage/cell-of-origin and chromatin-state marker (loss marks MPNST progression) rather than a directly druggable transcription factor target.
SPP1 is a secreted marker of tumor severity mainly from macrophages (MAC-3) with autocrine SCP signaling; no approved SPP1 inhibitors exist clinically.
SPRED1 is a RAS/MAPK-pathway tumour suppressor lost or mutated, not a druggable target; loss classifies tumours, doesn't guide inhibitor design.
SPRED1/2 are tumour suppressors whose loss (not an inhibitable protein) phenocopies NF1 loss in Schwann-lineage cells; loss status is more useful as a classifier/marker than a drug target.
Src is directly druggable by dasatinib, a clinical-stage/approved SFK inhibitor, acting on NF2-null meningioma tumour cells; NF2 loss defines the disease broadly.
STAT3 is directly druggable (FLLL32/JAK2-STAT3 inhibitor) and acts on both tumor Schwann cells and macrophages, with Schwann-cell/macrophage proliferation as the dominant mechanism.

Survivin is overexpressed in VS and best used as a pharmacodynamic/expression marker; no direct survivin inhibitor is credible, unlike EGFR/ErbB2 drugs (e.g. lapatinib) acting on schwannoma tumour cells.

mutation_context: SUZ12 (or EED) inactivating mutation causing PRC2 loss-of-function, found in ~70-90% of high-grade/malignant MPNST but not other NF1 manifestations
annotation_note: SUZ12 loss (PRC2 inactivation, H3K27me3 loss) is a diagnostic/subtyping marker for MPNST, not a direct drug target; no inhibitor restores a tumour-suppressor deletion.
Simvastatin is an approved HMGCR inhibitor acting on vascular wall inflammation/oxidative stress and MMP-9 in aneurysm, relevant to all Nf1+/- vasculopathy, not tumor cells.
TBK1 is a druggable kinase with clinical-stage inhibitors; acts directly on NF2-null schwannoma cells (e.g. via Hippo/YAP survival signaling), not restricted to a subgenotype or the microenvironment.

TEAD auto-palmitoylation inhibitors directly inhibit proliferation and induce apoptosis in NF2-null schwannoma/meningioma tumour cells, a genuine direct drug mechanism relevant to all NF2-SWN patients.

TEAD1 is a druggable Hippo-pathway transcription factor (TEAD/YAP-TAZ inhibitors in clinical development) acting directly on MPNST/schwannoma tumor cells, relevant across NF1/NF2 patients, not a specific subclone marker.
TGFB1 is a secreted ligand druggable by neutralizing antibodies, acting on stromal/fibrotic microenvironment (SSPCs, fibrosis) rather than the Schwann-cell tumor lineage itself.
TβR1 kinase is directly druggable (PRG-N-01 blocks TβR1-RKIP in Schwann tumor cells), but a second mechanism shows TGFβR signaling driving macrophage proliferation, a stromal/TME effect.
Explicitly proposed as a monitoring/pharmacodynamic biomarker in fibroblasts and plasma, not a drug target; where relevant it reflects fibroblast/stromal rather than Schwann-cell biology.
TRAIL-R2 is a direct pro-apoptotic surface receptor upregulated and engaged by fimepinostat in schwannoma tumor cells, not merely a stratification marker or stromal target.

TNFR1 is downregulated by fimepinostat in schwannoma tumour cells themselves (non-vestibular and vestibular models), a druggable node in pro-apoptotic signaling, not a TME or genotype-restricted marker.

mutation_context: TP53 inactivating mutation/deletion in TP53-altered MPNST, a subset of NF1-associated MPNST (not present in benign neurofibromas or germline NF1 loss)
annotation_note: TP53 loss is undruggable directly and serves as a diagnostic/prognostic marker restricted to the TP53-altered MPNST subset, acting tumor-cell-intrinsically.
VEGFA is directly druggable (bevacizumab shows clinical efficacy in NF2 schwannoma) and acts via anti-angiogenic effects on tumor endothelium, not the Schwann-lineage tumor cell.
VEGFR2 is a validated druggable kinase (cabozantinib etc.); mechanism here is anti-angiogenic, acting on tumor endothelium/microenvironment, not the Schwann-lineage tumor cell.

WNT/β-catenin is druggable (e.g., porcupine, β-catenin/BCL9 disruptors, tankyrase inhibitors) and acts directly on MPNST Schwann-lineage tumor cells, not stroma, in all NF1-MPNST regardless of genotype.
WWTR1/TAZ is an undruggable transcriptional coactivator activated by Hippo pathway loss in Schwann-lineage MPNST cells, more useful as a pathway-activity marker than a direct drug target.

Canonical Wnt/β-catenin drives Schwann-cell-intrinsic MPNST transformation; pathway is druggable (e.g., porcupine/tankyrase/GSK3B inhibitors), acting on tumor cells, not restricted to a specific genotype.
ICG-001 directly inhibits CBP-β-catenin interaction in Merlin-deficient meningioma tumor cells downstream of germline NF2 loss, a credible tumor-cell-intrinsic pharmacological approach.
XPO1 is a nuclear export protein with an approved inhibitor (selinexor) acting directly on MPNST tumor cells, relevant broadly, not a specific subtype.
YAP acts downstream of merlin loss in tumour cells itself; druggable indirectly via CUDC907, which lowers YAP and reduces schwannoma/meningioma cell viability.
TEAD has clinical-stage direct inhibitors (e.g. VT3989); acts on Schwann-lineage tumor cells downstream of germline Merlin/NF2 loss present in essentially all NF2-SWN patients.
TEAD palmitoylation inhibitors directly and druggably block YAP/TAZ-TEAD signaling in NF2-null Schwann-lineage tumor cells themselves, relevant across essentially all NF2-driven tumors.
ZNF331 appears as an epigenetically silenced candidate tumor suppressor in MPNST, not a druggable node, best used as a diagnostic/prognostic methylation biomarker.
